newsitem.title: INDIA: Arafat in India for non-aligned meeting.
newsitem.headline: Arafat in India for non-aligned meeting.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat has arrived in the Indian capital for a meeting of the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM), a Palestinian embassy spokesman said on Monday.
He said Arafat, who arrived overnight on a one-day visit to India, was due to address NAM foreign ministers later on Monday in a special plenary session.
Conference officials said the movement was considering adopting a special declaration on the Palestinian issue after Arafat's speech. The Palestinians hold the vice presidency of the 113-member NAM.

Arafat's surprise visit to New Delhi was expected to dominate the first day of the NAM meeting and push the stalled Israeli-Palestinian peace process to the top of its agenda, which will otherwise focus on U.N. reform and disarmament.

A draft of the meeting's conclusions said the movement's members "reaffirmed their full support for the legitimate struggle of the Palestinian people to secure their inalienable rights to self-determination and independence and reiterated their demand for the withdrawal of Israel from all occupied Palestinian and other Arab lands, including Jerusalem".
The draft, obtained by Reuters, was expected to be finalised and adopted by NAM ministers on Tuesday.

The Palestinian ambassador to India said senior officials of NAM member-states had already approved a draft resolution calling for a special session of the United Nations General Assembly on the Palestinian issue.
Middle East peace talks were halted after Israel began work last month on a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem, sparking daily clashes between Palestinians and Israeli troops.
Arafat was also scheduled to meet Indian President Shankar Dayal Sharma, Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda and Foreign Minister Inder Kumar Gujral on Monday.
